high.title: BPS: July 2026 Records Deflation of 0.14%
high.summary: Indonesia's Central Statistics Agency (BPS) recorded a monthly deflation of 0.14% in July 2026, with annual inflation at 2.88% (YoY) and year-to-date inflation at 1.65%. The deflation was primarily driven by the food, beverages, and tobacco category, which contracted 0.89% and contributed -0.26% to overall monthly price movement. This data is critical for investors as it signals easing price pressures and may influence Bank Indonesia's future monetary policy decisions.

high.title: BPS Reports July 2026 Deflation of 0.14%
high.summary: Indonesia's Central Statistics Agency (BPS) recorded a monthly deflation of 0.14% in July 2026, while year-on-year inflation stood at 2.88% and year-to-date inflation at 1.65%. The primary driver of deflation was the food, beverages, and tobacco group, which contributed a 0.26% deflationary impact. This data is critical for investors as it signals easing price pressures and could influence Bank Indonesia's future monetary policy decisions.

high.title: BULOG Receives Full Financial Support from Government for Food Self-Sufficiency
high.summary: The government has issued Bapanas Regulation No. 3 dated July 29, 2026, significantly increasing BULOG's assignment margin to 7% (equivalent to Rp 970 per unit), up dramatically from the previous margin of approximately Rp 50. This major policy shift strengthens BULOG's financial capacity as the national food operator and is expected to create fiscal efficiency for the state. The move represents a significant regulatory change in Indonesia's food supply chain management with broad implications for the agriculture and commodities sectors.

high.title: OJK Reveals Evidence of IHSG Recovery
high.summary: The Financial Services Authority (OJK) reported bullish signals in Indonesia's capital market, with the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) gaining 10.51% month-to-date through July 31, 2026, closing at 6,236.13. This follows a sharp correction where the IHSG had fallen to 5,643.19 at the end of Q2 2026, representing a 19.93% quarter-to-quarter decline amid global uncertainty and investor portfolio rebalancing. The recovery signal is significant for investors as it suggests renewed market confidence after a prolonged downturn.

high.title: IHSG Reverses to Slight Decline to 6,234 in Session I
high.summary: The IHSG reversed earlier gains to close the first trading session of Monday slightly lower at 6,234.29, down 0.03%, in line with broader weakness across Asian markets. The index had briefly reached a high of 6,273.32 during morning trading before pulling back, with total transaction value reaching Rp 7.68 trillion. This intraday volatility reflects ongoing uncertainty among investors despite the broader monthly recovery trend.

high.title: Indonesia's Finance Minister Tells World Bank & IMF: 'I'm the Most Unlucky Minister in the World'
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa recounted facing a series of major challenges since taking office, including large-scale protests, negative sentiment from international rating agencies, and external geopolitical shocks such as the outbreak of the Iran war. Despite these pressures, he affirmed that Indonesia's economic fundamentals remain solid, underpinned by strong fiscal and monetary policy frameworks. This statement is significant for investors assessing Indonesia's macroeconomic stability and sovereign risk profile.

high.title: Russian Banks Begin Cash Crisis: Liquidity Crunch Threatens Government Bond Market
high.summary: Russian banks are facing a significant ruble liquidity squeeze, with approximately 2 trillion rubles (around USD 25.2 billion) withdrawn from the banking system since the start of the year, according to Sberbank's CFO. This limits banks' capacity to purchase government bonds needed to finance Russia's growing budget deficit driven by war spending. For Indonesian investors, this signals escalating financial stress in Russia with potential spillover effects on global commodity markets and emerging market sentiment.

high.title: Trump Intervenes to Help Japan Strengthen Yen Against US Dollar
high.summary: Japan's Ministry of Finance conducted a coordinated yen-buying intervention with the US Treasury starting Friday (July 31), after the yen weakened to 163.73 per USD — its weakest level in four decades. The coordinated action pushed the yen back to around 157.57-157.70, with Japan signaling readiness for further intervention if needed. This development is highly relevant to Indonesian investors as yen volatility impacts regional currency dynamics, Japanese investment flows into Indonesia, and broader Asian FX market stability.

high.title: Indonesia's Imports Surge Sharply – Here's the Main Driver
high.summary: Indonesia's total import value surged 34.27% year-on-year in June 2026, reaching US$25.9 billion, according to BPS (Statistics Indonesia). The primary driver was a massive 105.15% increase in oil and gas (migas) imports worth US$4.56 billion, while non-oil and gas imports rose 25.05% to US$21.35 billion. This significant import spike has direct implications for Indonesia's trade balance and current account deficit, which could pressure the Rupiah.

high.title: OJK Chief Reveals Condition of Indonesia's Financial Sector Amid Global Turmoil
high.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi stated that Indonesia's financial services sector remains stable despite ongoing global uncertainty stemming from geopolitical conflicts and a global economic slowdown. Renewed tensions in the Middle East following a failed US-Iran ceasefire in early July 2026 have pushed global oil prices higher and increased global risk premiums. Investors should monitor potential spillover effects on Indonesian markets, banking sector liquidity, and commodity-linked assets.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Rises to Rp 2,610,000 per Gram
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold rose by Rp 7,000 per gram to Rp 2,610,000 on Monday, August 3, 2026. However, the price remains within a declining trend over the past week and month, having retreated from a recent high of Rp 2,670,000. This is relevant for retail and institutional investors using gold as a hedge against inflation and currency risk.

medium.title: KAI's Profit Drops Sharply in First Half of 2026 Despite Revenue Growth
medium.summary: State-owned railway company PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) reported a sharp decline in net profit to Rp 314.03 billion in H1 2026, down from Rp 1.18 trillion in the same period last year, representing a drop of over 73%. Despite this, revenue grew 6.6% year-on-year to Rp 17.96 trillion, suggesting rising operational costs are squeezing margins. This is significant for investors and analysts monitoring the performance of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in Indonesia's transport sector.

medium.title: Bulog Confirms Free Nutritious Meals Program Uses Premium Products, Not Subsidized Goods
medium.summary: Bulog's CEO confirmed that all food supplies for the government's Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program consist of premium-grade products, explicitly excluding subsidized rice (SPHP) and Minyakita cooking oil. This clarification comes after the Head of the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) announced investigations into MBG kitchens potentially misusing subsidized goods. The statement has implications for subsidy allocation, food supply chain integrity, and the overall fiscal cost of the MBG program.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Rises to Rp 2,610,000 per Gram
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold price increased by Rp 7,000 per gram to Rp 2,610,000 on Monday, August 3, 2026. Over the past week, prices ranged between Rp 2,610,000 and Rp 2,623,000, while the monthly range was Rp 2,601,000 to Rp 2,670,000 per gram. This is relevant for commodity investors and retail savers who track gold as a safe-haven asset in Indonesia.

medium.title: Thailand Offers Quality Rice Supply, Seeks to Import Indonesian Fertilizer
medium.summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul proposed deeper agricultural cooperation with Indonesia during a bilateral meeting with President Prabowo, offering Thailand as a reliable supplier of high-quality rice and requesting expanded imports of Thai agricultural products including meat, dairy, and farming machinery. Indonesia is also being asked to increase imports of Thai agricultural and livestock products. This bilateral negotiation could impact Indonesia's domestic rice and agriculture sector, as well as fertilizer export opportunities for Indonesian producers.

medium.title: BGN Chief Threatens to Fire Free Nutritious Meal Program Kitchen Staff Who Violate SOPs
medium.summary: The newly appointed head of the National Nutrition Agency (BGN), Sudaryono, declared a zero-tolerance policy on food safety violations and corruption within the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program following a food poisoning incident affecting hundreds of students at SMK Negeri 6 Semarang. He threatened immediate dismissal of kitchen staff found in violation of standard operating procedures. This development highlights ongoing operational and governance risks within the government's flagship MBG program, which has significant budgetary implications for the state.

medium.title: KAI's Profits Shrink Sharply: The Root Causes
medium.summary: State-owned railway company KAI recorded a significant decline in profitability in H1 2026, with pre-tax profit falling to Rp 842.69 billion and net profit dropping to Rp 314.03 billion, compared to Rp 1.86 trillion and Rp 1.18 trillion respectively in the same period last year. Despite revenue growing 6.6% year-on-year to Rp 17.96 trillion, the sharp profit compression raises concerns about rising costs and operational efficiency. This is relevant for investors tracking state-owned enterprise performance and infrastructure sector health.

medium.title: Power Outage: PLN Reveals Supply Disruption from Gandul to Cirendeu
medium.summary: State electricity company PLN reported a power supply disruption from the Gandul substation towards Cirendeu at 04:59 WIB, causing outages across several areas in greater Jakarta. PLN's Jakarta Raya regional unit stated that normalization efforts are underway while the root cause is still being investigated. The outage is notable for businesses and investors monitoring PLN's operational reliability and infrastructure stability in the capital region.

medium.title: IDX Introduces New 'P' Notation for Companies Not Meeting Free Float Requirements
medium.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) has begun displaying special notations on listed company codes within its Jakarta Automated Trading System (JATS), introducing the new 'P' notation for companies that have not met free float requirements, while removing the previous E, D, A, and S notations. The move is part of IDX's capital market reform agenda aimed at improving information transparency and strengthening investor protection. Investors should monitor their portfolios for stocks receiving the 'P' notation as it signals potential liquidity and governance concerns.

medium.title: Presidential Staff Office Clarifies Policy on Rare Earth Export Ban: Ban Applies Only to Primary Rare Earth Products
medium.summary: Indonesia's Presidential Staff Office (KSP) clarified that the rare earth element (REE) export ban applies only to rare earth as a primary product, not to mining commodities that contain rare earth as a byproduct or incidental element. This clarification follows disruptions to several mining companies whose exports were held up due to REE content inspections. The policy update is important for mining and commodities sector investors, as it reduces regulatory uncertainty and could restore export flows for affected companies.

medium.title: OJK Blocks 36,000 Bank Accounts Linked to Online Gambling Activities
medium.summary: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) has requested banks to apply enhanced due diligence (EDD) and/or block approximately 36,735 accounts suspected of being used for illegal online gambling (judol) and online scam activities. This is an increase from the previously reported 36,191 accounts, with data sourced from the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs. The ongoing crackdown signals tightening regulatory oversight on banking compliance and anti-money laundering (AML) enforcement, which may affect operational procedures across Indonesian banks.

medium.title: Minister of Villages: 'Red and White' Village Cooperatives to Drive Rural Economy
medium.summary: The Indonesian government is targeting the establishment of 30,000 Red and White Village/Kelurahan Cooperatives (KDKMP) this year, aimed at becoming distribution hubs for government assistance and stimulating rural economic growth and employment. The program was highlighted at a National Seminar in Makassar by Minister of Villages Yandri Susanto, organized in collaboration with 10 Village Associations. This initiative represents a significant rural economic development policy with potential impact on consumption patterns, logistics, and small-to-medium enterprise (SME) ecosystems in rural Indonesia.
